identity.title: Faint End of 1.3 mm Number Counts Revealed by ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: Band 6 observations were carried out targeting 20 star-forming galaxies at $z \sim 1.4$ in the Subaru/*XMM-Newton* Deep Survey field. In the observations, we serendipitously detect 15 sources

targets.name: 20 star-forming galaxies at z~1.4 in the SXDS field (serendipitous sources in their maps)

evidence.quote: We conducted ALMA band 6 observations toward 20 star-forming galaxies at $z \sim 1.4$ in the Subaru XMM/Newton Deep Survey (SXDS) field

distance_source.value: NIR spectroscopy with FMOS on Subaru

evidence.quote: We conducted ALMA band 6 observations toward 20 star-forming galaxies at $z \sim 1.4$ in the Subaru XMM/Newton Deep Survey (SXDS) field

question.value: What is the faint end (sub-mJy) of the 1.3 mm number counts, and how much of the extragalactic background light is resolved into sources?

evidence.quote: In this letter, we present the faint end of number counts at 1.3 mm revealed by ALMA band 6 observations.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00648.S.
We present the faint end of number counts at 1.3 mm (238 GHz) obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four groups with LO 231.198, 236.168, 240.380, 244.166 GHz; 3-4 spectral windows of 1875 MHz each

evidence.quote: The local oscillator frequencies for the four groups were 231.198 GHz, 236.168 GHz, 240.380 GHz, and 244.166 GHz (typical frequency of 238 GHz).
The targets were divided into four groups with different spectral settings to observe the redshifted CO(5–4) line as efficiently as possible.
with 23–25 antennas in the extended configuration during the ALMA Cycle 0 session
each with on-source observing time of 8–15 minutes
The observations were carried out in August 9th, 11th, 15th, and 26th, 2012
whose redshifts were obtained by near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy with the Fibre Multi-Object Spectro-graph (cite: kimu10) on the Subaru telescope

what.value: Literature number counts (SCUBA 850um, LABOCA 870um, AzTEC 1.1mm, ALMA 870um) for comparison

evidence.quote: we plot number counts obtained by SCUBA 850 $\mu$m (cite: knud08), LABOCA 870 $\mu$m (cite: joha11), AzTEC 1.1 mm (cite: scot12)

what.value: EBL at 1.3 mm of 14-18 Jy deg^-2 from COBE

evidence.loc: Contribution to the Extragalactic Background Light
evidence.quote: The EBL at 1.3 mm based on the measurements by the *Cosmic Background Explorer* satellite is 14–18 Jy deg$^{-2}$ (cite: puge96; fixs98).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Model counts from shim12, beth12, dacu13 compared with ALMA counts

evidence.quote: We compare the 1.3 mm counts with recent model predictions with different approaches by (cite: shim12), (cite: beth12), and (cite: dacu13).
Ganymede, Callisto, and Uranus were observed as a flux calibrator.

primary_beam_correction.value: Source extraction in maps uncorrected for primary beam; flux corrected afterwards; primary beam FWHM 26"

evidence.quote: Because the source extraction is conducted in the maps uncorrected for primary beam attenuation

what.value: Flux scaling to 1.3 mm uses modified blackbody with beta=1.5, T=35 K at z=2.5

evidence.quote: spectral index of $\beta = 1.5$ and dust temperature of 35 K (cite: kova06; copp08) located at $z = 2.5$ (cite: chap05; yun12)

unstated_but_needed: CASA version and reduction procedure (done with ARC staff)
Imaging parameters: weighting, cell size, image size, deconvolution, continuum channels
Source-finding algorithm and how spurious detection rate was derived
Synthesized beam and rms per map

method.value: Detect sources at >=3.8 sigma in 20 maps uncorrected for primary beam, excluding targets

evidence.quote: We detect 15 sources (excluding the target sources) in the 20 maps with the raw flux density (uncorrected for the primary beam attenuation)

method.value: Subtract >=3.5 sigma sources, inject flux-scaled synthesized beam at random positions, recover within 1.0" at >=3.8 sigma; 1000 repeats per source

evidence.quote: We repeat this 1000 times for the raw flux density of each source.

method.value: Per map, find radius within which source is detected at >=3.8 sigma given PB-corrected rms

evidence.quote: we find a distance from the map center within which the source is detected at $\ge$$3.8 \sigma$ in the raw map uncorrected for primary beam attenuation

method.value: Weight each source by (1 - C_spurious)/completeness/effective area; Poisson errors at 84.13% confidence

evidence.quote: The upper and lower errors are calculated for each source from Poisson confidence limits of 84.13%, which correspond to $1 \sigma$ for Gaussian statistics (cite: gehr86)

validation.value: Compared counts from 4.0 sigma subsample; consistent

evidence.quote: We also plot the number counts created by using 6 $\ge$$4.0 \sigma$ sources to see the effect of the detection threshold.

method.value: Sum corrected flux of >=3.8 sigma sources and divide by COBE EBL

evidence.loc: Contribution to the Extragalactic Background Light
evidence.quote: Therefore, we have resolved $\sim$80% of the EBL into discrete sources
we serendipitously detect 15 sources ($\ge$$3.8 \sigma$, $S_{\rm 1.3\ mm} = 0.15$–0.61 mJy)
The completeness for the 15 sources ranges from 77% to 100%.
The flux ratio calculated for each source in this simulation is 1.00–1.14.

evidence.loc: Contribution to the Extragalactic Background Light
evidence.quote: is $\sim$13 Jy deg$^{-2}$

evidence.loc: Contribution to the Extragalactic Background Light
evidence.quote: we have resolved $\sim$80% of the EBL into discrete sources

findings_qualitative.value: Counts consistent with flux-scaled 850/870 um lensing-cluster counts and with three models; no turnover seen at faint end

evidence.quote: However, our data points at fainter flux range do not show such turnover.

claims.hypothesis: Sub-mJy 1.3 mm counts match lensing-cluster counts at submm
claims.finding: Both wavelengths trace the same faint population

evidence.quote: The ALMA 1.3 mm counts are consistent with those counts, suggesting that both wavelengths trace the same population at faint end.

claims.hypothesis: Sub-mJy sources are normal star-forming galaxies rather than classical SMGs
claims.finding: Sources more like normal star-forming galaxies

evidence.quote: suggest that these sub-mJy populations are more like ‘normal’ star-forming galaxies than ‘classical’ SMGs

claims.hypothesis: Faint sources resolve much of the EBL
claims.experiment: Sum corrected fluxes vs COBE EBL

evidence.quote: $\sim$80% of the extragalactic background light at 1.3 mm is resolved into individual sources.

limitations_admitted.value: Counts from targeted fields may show excess; comparison with 870 um counts not quantitative

evidence.quote: We note that number counts derived from targeted observations may show an excess of source counts.

referee_caveats_inferred: Fields targeted at z~1.4 galaxies may bias counts via clustering
Flux scaling from 850/870 um assumes single SED
